references.text: The institution of Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread in Egypt. The Passover lamb was to be slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the month ([ref:2 Mos 12:6-20|Exodus 12:6-20]). Luke refers back to this when he says that the Day of Unleavened Bread came, when the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.

The command to eat unleavened bread for seven days, from the fourteenth day of the first month ([ref:2 Mos 12:15-18|Exodus 12:15-18]). The expression "the Day of Unleavened Bread" in Luke points directly to this feast.

The Lord's Passover is celebrated on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight ([ref:2 Mos 23:5|Leviticus 23:5]). This is the fixed time setting for the Passover celebration that Luke refers to.

Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread are mentioned together in [ref:3 Mos 23:5-6|Leviticus 23:5-6]. Passover is on the 14th day of the first month, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread begins on the 15th. Luke uses these terms interchangeably, as was common in Jesus' time.
In [ref:4 Mos 28:16-17|Numbers 28:16-17], Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread are closely linked, which explains Luke's connection of the two in this verse.

Moses commands that the Passover lamb be slaughtered at the place the Lord chooses ([ref:5 Mos 16:1-6|Deuteronomy 16:1-6]). Jerusalem was this place, and it is there that Jesus sends the disciples to prepare for Passover.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 26:17|Matthew 26:17] tells the same story: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked where he wanted them to make preparations for the Passover meal.

The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 14:12|Mark 14:12] explicitly mentions that it was the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, "when they sacrificed the Passover lamb." This corresponds exactly to Luke's wording.
In [ref:Joh 13:1|John 13:1], John places the last meal before the Feast of Passover. John's timeline complements the Synoptic Gospels' account of the preparations for Passover.

Paul writes: "For our Passover lamb has been sacrificed, Christ" ([ref:1 Kor 5:7|1 Corinthians 5:7]). The slaughter of the Passover lamb that Luke mentions points forward to Christ's sacrificial death as the true Passover Lamb.
